subject: environmental-science
title: ISO 14067 and Product Footprints
welcome_lead: From cradle to grave — quantify the carbon in your kettle, croissant or car.
meta_desc: A-Level Environmental Science adventure on ISO 14067 product carbon footprint methodology.
final_note: Every product has a hidden carbon story — LCA reveals it.

concepts.def: International standard for product carbon footprint quantification (2018).
Cradle-to-grave inventory of inputs and outputs across a product's life.
Quantified reference for comparison (e.g., 1 km driven, 1 L of milk).
LCA scope from raw materials to factory gate.
Emissions associated with materials, construction and end-of-life.
Method of dividing emissions between co-products (mass, economic, energy).

walkthroughs.body_html: ISO 14040 defines four stages: goal and scope, inventory, impact assessment, interpretation.
Cradle-to-grave includes use and disposal; cradle-to-gate stops at manufacturing.
Beef: ~60 kg CO₂e kg⁻¹ protein. Lentils: ~1 kg CO₂e kg⁻¹ protein. Choices matter.

numericals.q: If 1 kg beef emits 60 kg CO₂e and 1 kg lentils 1 kg CO₂e, beef factor (×) compared to lentils is?

free_texts.q: ISO standard number for product carbon footprint (five digits, no spaces).
